record.title: Period-six conjecture for misère Sprouts
record.statement: Let $S_p^-$ denote the misère version of Sprouts starting with $p$ spots. **Period-six conjecture for misère Sprouts.** The first player has a winning strategy in $S_p^-$ if and only if $p$ is equal to $0$, $4$ or $5$ modulo $6$, except if $p=1$ or $4$. The paper presents this conjecture after listing computed values through $S_{17}^-$. Its general validity is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Julien Lemoine and Simon Viennot, “Analysis of misere Sprouts game with reduced canonical trees”, arXiv:0908.4407 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.4407

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2009).

record.title: Ahmed–Kullmann–Snevily's one-count bound for good partitions
record.statement:
For $t\geqslant 3$, let $S(t)$ be the set of good partitions considered in the paper, and for $B\in S(t)$ let $n_1(B)$ denote the number of $1$'s in $B$. **One-count bound conjecture.** For every $B\in S(t)$ and every $B'\in S(t-1)$,

$$
n_1(B')\leqslant n_1(B)\leqslant w(2;3,t-1)+2t.
$$

The claim is an observed property of good partitions in the computed range and is presented as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the paper excerpt.
record.source_name: Tanbir Ahmed, Oliver Kullmann and Hunter Snevily, “On the van der Waerden numbers w(2;3,t)”, arXiv:1102.5433 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.5433

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2011).

record.title: Parity conjecture for the number of square rectangulations
record.statement:
Let $t_m$ denote the total number of rectangulations of a square with $m$ tiles, and write $n$ for a positive integer. **Parity conjecture.**

$$
t_n\equiv 1\!\!\mod 2
$$

if $n=8k+1$ or $n=8k+4$; otherwise,

$$
t_n\equiv 0\!\!\mod 2.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the computed sequence of total rectangulation counts and was stated as unproved in the source, which gives partial results concerning symmetry.
record.source_name: Jim Conant and Tim Michaels, “On the number of tilings of a square by rectangles”, arXiv:1204.5734 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.5734

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

record.title: Differentiability conjecture for mixed transport-diffusion quantum graph semigroups
record.statement:
Let $athsf{E}_t\not=\emptyset$ be the set of transport edges and $athsf{E}_d\not=\emptyset$ the set of diffusive edges. Let $A_{P,L}$ generate the semigroup $T(t)=e^{tA_{P,L}}$ on the state space $X$, with boundary conditions determined by $P$ and $L$. Let $T$ denote the length of the longest path contained in $athsf{E}_t$, computed while taking into account possibly coupled boundary conditions. For transport-supported initial data, the semigroup shifts the profile without smoothing until it reaches an endpoint.

**Differentiability conjecture.** If $athsf{E}_d\not=\emptyset$, then the semigroup is differentiable for every $t>T$; equivalently, for every $x\in X$, the map

$$
(T,\infty)\ni t\longmapsto T(t)x\in X
$$

is differentiable.

The transport component prevents immediate smoothing, analyticity, and immediate differentiability before profiles reach diffusive edges. The conjecture predicts that the diffusive part smooths the semigroup after the maximal transport-path length, even when the boundary conditions couple transport and diffusion components.
record.source_name: Amru Hussein and Delio Mugnolo, “Quantum graphs with mixed dynamics: the transport/diffusion case”, arXiv:1209.5564 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.5564

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2012).

record.title: The 1089 graph divisibility conjecture for reverse multiples
record.statement:
Let $g$ and $k$ be parameters of a $(g,k)$-reverse multiple and let its associated Young graph be the **$(g,k)$ Young graph**. The **1089 graph** is the Young graph isomorphic to the $(10,4)$ and $(10,9)$ Young graphs.

**1089 graph conjecture.** The $(g,k)$ Young graph is isomorphic to the 1089 graph if and only if $k+1$ divides $g$.

The conjecture would explain the many occurrences of the 1089 graph in the computed examples; it is known when $k=g-1$, but the general case remains open.
record.source_name: N. J. A. Sloane, “2178 And All That”, arXiv:1307.0453 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.0453

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2013).

record.title: Forbidden graphs for hereditary equality of domination numbers have values 3 and 2
record.statement:
Let ${\cal F}$ be a finite forbidden set as in the finite forbidden-subgraph conjecture, and let $\gamma(F)$ and $\gamma_e(F)$ denote the domination number and exponential domination number of a graph $F$. **Refined forbidden-set conjecture.** The set ${\cal F}$ can be chosen so that

$$
\gamma(F)=3 \quad\text{and}\quad \gamma_e(F)=2
$$

for every graph $F$ in ${\cal F}$. This gives a proposed normalization of the obstructions in the finite characterization, requiring each forbidden graph to witness the same discrepancy between the two domination parameters; no resolution is given in the paper.
record.source_name: Michael A. Henning, Simon Jäger and Dieter Rautenbach, “Hereditary Equality of Domination and Exponential Domination”, arXiv:1605.05056 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.05056

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: Effective Larsen–Shalev conjecture for automorphic word maps
record.statement:
Let $w$ be a nonempty reduced word in $d$ distinct variables, and let $N(w),\eta(w)>0$ be the constants in the Larsen–Shalev conjecture for automorphic word maps.

**Effective Larsen–Shalev conjecture.** The constants $N(w)$ and $\eta(w)$ can be computed algorithmically from the word $w$ as input.

This is explicitly described as a slightly stronger version of the preceding conjecture. It would provide effective quantitative control for automorphic word maps, and the source uses it as the hypothesis for deriving an algorithmic statement about solvable radicals.
record.source_name: Alexander Bors, “Fibers of automorphic word maps and an application to composition factors”, arXiv:1608.00131 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.00131

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2016).

record.title: The three-partition conjecture for knapsack partitions
record.statement: Let $K(n)$ be the set of knapsack partitions of $n$, and let $P_n$ be the convex hull of the integer partitions of $n$. **The three-partition conjecture.** The majority of partitions in $K(n)$ that are not vertices of $P_n$ are convex combinations of three partitions of $n$. The conjecture is motivated by computed ratios involving the number of vertices, knapsack partitions, and Metropolis 2-partitions; no proof is given.
record.source_name: Vladimir A. Shlyk, “Number of Vertices of the Polytope of Integer Partitions and Factorization of the Partitioned Number”, arXiv:1805.07989 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.07989

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: Blocker-family conjecture for maximal independent sets
record.statement:
Let $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$. **Blocker-family conjecture.** There exist $k$ and $\tau>0$ such that, for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with a maximal independent set of size $\alpha n$, there are disjoint subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq V(G)$ satisfying

$$
|A_i|=k\quad\text{for all }i,
$$

$$
\left|\bigcup_i A_i\right|=\tau n,
$$

and every maximal independent set in $G$ intersects every set $A_i$. This proposed blocker structure is intended to imply the preceding random-subgraph conjectures, but the authors explicitly say that it may be too strong and that they found no counterexample.
record.source_name: Ehud Friedgut, Gil Kalai and Guy Kindler, “The success probability in Lionel Levine's hat problem is strictly decreasing with the number of players, and this is related to interesting questions regarding Hamming powers of Kneser graphs and independent sets in random subgraphs”, arXiv:2103.01541 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01541

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The cycle-barbell-theta girth conjecture for star friends-and-strangers graphs
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a connected graph with finite girth, let $\mathcal C$ be the set of cycle subgraphs of $\mathsf{FS}(X,\textsf{Star}_n)$ that achieve its girth, and for each $C\in\mathcal C$ let $X_C$ be the path-induced subgraph of $X$ by $C$. Set

$$
\mathcal X=\{X_C\}_{C\in\mathcal C}.
$$

The **cycle-barbell-theta girth conjecture** asserts that some $X_C\in\mathcal X$ is isomorphic to a cycle, barbell, or theta graph, and that the girth can be computed by taking the corresponding sequence of swaps around that graph. The statement is a proposed structural characterization of shortest cycles in these friends-and-strangers graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Ryan Jeong, “On the Diameters of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs”, arXiv:2201.00665 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.00665

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Equal orbit-growth constants imply equal generating-function denominators
record.statement:
Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be primitive necklaces, and let $c_{P_1}$ and $c_{P_2}$ be their orbit-growth constants when these constants exist. Let $H_{P_i}(x)$ denote the limiting level size generating function associated with $P_i$.

**Equal-constant denominator conjecture.** For any two primitive necklaces $P_1$ and $P_2$, if $c_{P_1}=c_{P_2}$, then $H_{P_1}(x)$ and $H_{P_2}(x)$ have the same denominator.

The conjecture is motivated by computed examples in which equal orbit-growth constants accompany equal denominators, while the paper does not provide a general proof or disproof. It therefore remains open.
record.source_name: A. J. Harris and Son Nguyen, “Bulgarian Solitaire: A new representation for depth generating functions”, arXiv:2308.05321 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05321

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: Schröder enumeration conjecture for the $\underline{23}1$ sorting class
record.statement:
Let $\text{SC}_{\underline{23}1}$ be the vincular-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map, let $\text{Sort}_n(\text{SC}_{\underline{23}1})$ denote its sorting class in $\mathfrak S_n$, and let $S_{n-1}$ denote the corresponding Schröder number. **Schröder enumeration conjecture.** The sorting class is enumerated by

$$
|\text{Sort}_n(\text{SC}_{\underline{23}1})|=S_{n-1}.
$$

The first ten computed terms agree with OEIS sequence A006318, the Schröder numbers, motivating this enumeration conjecture. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: William Zhao, “Stack-sorting with Stacks Avoiding Vincular Patterns”, arXiv:2410.17057 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Eventual periodicity of combinatorial zero mutable Laurent polynomial counts
record.statement:
For positive integers $a,b$, let $\textup{ZMLP}_{\textup{comb}}(a,b)$ be the combinatorially defined set of pairs of partitions used to characterize zero mutable Laurent polynomials on rectangular triangles.

**Eventual-periodicity conjecture.**
1. For each $a\in\mathbb N$ there exists $b_0\in\mathbb N$ such that for all $b\geq b_0$, the number $|\textup{ZMLP}_{\textup{comb}}(a,b)|$ depends only on $b$ modulo $a$.
2. For each $k\in\mathbb N$ there exists $a_0\in\mathbb N$ such that for all $a\geq a_0$, $|\textup{ZMLP}_{\textup{comb}}(a,a+k)|$ depends only on $a$ modulo $k$.

The conjecture is motivated by computed tables for large rectangular triangles. It predicts eventual modular periodicity of the combinatorial upper bound, not directly of the number of zero mutable Laurent polynomials; the supplied text gives no proof.
record.source_name: Tim Gräfnitz, “Smoothings from zero mutable Laurent polynomials via log resolutions and divisorial extractions”, arXiv:2503.18661 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: The intersection-polynomial determination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $w$ be a word, let $p_w(x)$ be its intersection polynomial, and let $h(w)$ be the dimension of its $\ell$-singular-vector space. **The intersection-polynomial determination conjecture.**
1. The number $h(w)$ depends only on $p_w(x)$: if $p_{w_1}(x)=p_{w_2}(x)$, then $h(w_1)=h(w_2)$.
2. One has $h(w)=1$ if and only if the intersection polynomial of $w$ is a product of polynomials of the form

$$
\frac{x^n-1}{x-1}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computed examples of configuration-connected words of lengths through $10$; its first part is noted to imply the conjecture that admissibility can be dropped. No resolution is stated.
record.source_name: Andrei Grigorev and Evgeny Mukhin, “On representations of quantum affine sl_2”, arXiv:2505.11605 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11605

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

record.title: Homotopy conjecture for 2-total cut complexes of powers of cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_n^p$ denote the $p$th power of the cycle graph $C_n$, and let $\Delta_2^t(C_n^p)$ be its 2-total cut complex.

**The 2-total cut complex conjecture.** For $p\ge 3$ and $n\ge 3p+1$,

$$
\Delta_2^t(C_n^p)\simeq \mathbb{S}^{n-4}.
$$

This conjecture is based on computed homology groups for powers of cycles and predicts a single-sphere homotopy type in the stated range. The source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Yufeng Shen, Zhiyu Song, Fenglin Yu, Leopold Wuhan Zhou and Jingqi Zhuang, “Homotopy Type of Total Cut Complexes of Squared Cycle Graphs”, arXiv:2510.22574 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22574

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

record.title: The rank-three transversal matroid half-plane-property conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a transversal matroid of rank $3$. Its basis generating polynomial is the sum of the monomials corresponding to the bases of $M$.

**Rank-three transversal matroid conjecture.** Every rank-$3$ transversal matroid has the half-plane property.

The conjecture is motivated by numerical experiments and by the fact that the paper proves the half-plane property only for a subclass of transversal matroids, called nice transversal matroids. The authors report no known counterexample, but do not provide a proof.
record.source_name: Young-Bin Choe, James G. Oxley, Alan D. Sokal and David G. Wagner, “Homogeneous multivariate polynomials with the half-plane property”, arXiv:math/0202034 (2002).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0202034

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2002). “However, this conjecture is false, since the matroid $F_7^{-3}$ is strongly base-orderable but does not have the half-plane property (Example .”

record.title: The Schubert-union conjecture for higher weights of Grassmann codes
record.statement: Let $G(l,m)$ be a Grassmann variety and let its associated Grassmann code have higher weights. A **Schubert union** is a union of Schubert varieties in the Grassmann variety. **Schubert-union conjecture.** The answer to Question (Q5) of Section is always affirmative; equivalently, the higher weights of the Grassmann codes are always computed by Schubert unions. The preceding theorem establishes the corresponding maximal-dimension result for linear sections, and the conjecture extends this phenomenon to all higher weights of Grassmann codes. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Johan P. Hansen, Trygve Johnsen and Kristian Ranestad, “Schubert Unions in Grassmann Varieties”, arXiv:math/0503121 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503121

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2005).

record.title: Nonnegative derivatives of the chromatic polynomial at maxmaxflow
record.statement: Let $G$ be a loopless graph with maxmaxflow $\Lambda$, and let $P_G(q)$ be its chromatic polynomial. **Maxmaxflow derivative-positivity conjecture.** The polynomial $P_G(q)/q$ and all its derivatives are nonnegative at $q=\Lambda$; the same then holds for $P_G(q)$ and all its derivatives. The source derives this as a consequence of the preceding half-plane conjecture and reports that the latter has counterexamples, so this conjecture is refuted as part of the same counterexample family.
record.source_name: Alan D. Sokal, “The multivariate Tutte polynomial (alias Potts model) for graphs and matroids”, arXiv:math/0503607 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503607

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2005). “STOP PRESS!!!} Gordon Royle (private communication) has found a family of counterexamples to Conjectures and ${}'$.”

record.title: Minimal-rank completion conjecture for bipartite chordal patterns
record.statement: Let a partial matrix have a bipartite graph whose vertices represent its rows and columns and whose edges represent specified entries. A fully specified submatrix is one in which every entry is specified, and a completion of rank $r$ is a matrix agreeing with all specified entries and having rank $r$. **Minimal-rank completion conjecture.** Suppose the bipartite graph is bipartite chordal, every fully specified submatrix has full rank, and every $k\times k$ submatrix has at most $(2k-r)r$ specified entries. Then there exists a completion of rank $r$. The conjecture proposes that bipartite chordality together with the stated density and nondegeneracy conditions is sufficient for a rank-$r$ completion; the preceding discussion establishes the result for $r=1$ and gives a counterexample without the bipartite-chordal hypothesis for $r\geq 2$.
record.source_name: Hugo J. Woerdeman, “A matrix and its inverse: revisting minimal rank completions”, arXiv:math/0608130 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

record.title: Stahl's real-rootedness conjecture for graph genus polynomials
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let

$$
\Gamma_G(x)=\sum_{k\geq 0}g_k(G)x^k
$$

be its genus polynomial, where $g_k(G)$ is the number of 2-cell embeddings of $G$ in an orientable surface of genus $k$.

**Stahl's real-rootedness conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the genus polynomial $\Gamma_G(x)$ has only real roots.

The conjecture was proposed by Stahl as a stronger property than log-concavity of the genus distribution. It was later disproved; the paper discusses counterexamples among graph genus polynomials, although it also notes an error in one previously proposed counterexample.
record.source_name: MacKenzie Carr, Varpreet Dhaliwal and Bojan Mohar, “Genus Polynomials of Cubic Graphs with Non-Real Roots”, arXiv:2212.09971 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2005–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0509207](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0509207).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09971

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2022). “It was further conjectured by Stahl that the genus polynomial of every graph has only real roots, however this was later disproved.”
